_comment: What each service's committed answers score UNDER THE CURRENT INSTRUMENT, pinned so the instrument cannot move underneath a published row. This is the comparator the L2 gate lane decides on, and it is deliberately not the recorded history number: a recorded score is what was measured on the day and never changes, while a comparator is what those same answers score today. ADR-016 is the reason the two differ at all. Changing a value here is a two-key act (AI Quality) and must state, in the PR body, which instrument change moved it and in which direction.
_why_deviation_in_either_direction_fails: A drop is the obvious regression. A RISE is the one this repo exists to catch: the m00b control gained three cases when ADR-016 moved p95 to suite level, with no improvement to any system, and a flattering control makes every later milestone unfalsifiable (CLAUDE.md). So the lane fails on any deviation and names the direction, rather than passing anything at-or-above.

highlights-agent.why_they_differ: The `cited_titles_in_fixture` tightening (PR #23) landed after m02 was tagged. It closed a vacuous groundedness pass — an empty citation list satisfied the assert — and cost the tools arm one case. The recorded 16/25 is what the instrument reported on the day and does not move; 15/25 is what these same answers score now. The control arm is unchanged at 17/25 under the same tightening, which is what makes it a tightening rather than a re-scoring.

control.why: The M01 prompt frozen as M02's control arm (ADR-021). Pinned beside the tools arm because the paired diff is the result, not the total — a comparator that moved on only one arm would silently change the delta.
